body:
To anyone curious, it's likely a problem of when (or rather, where) `connection.features` gets evaluated.

```python
await a_getattr(connection.features, "supports_json_field")
```

is executed in the following order:

```python
foo = connection.features
bar = a_getattr(foo, "supports_json_field")
await bar
```

Evaluating `connection.features` does the following:

1. Since `connection` is a `ConnectionProxy` instance, it first finds a default connection
2. It takes that connection and returns a `DatabaseFeatures` instance bound to it

That first step is tricky because it uses the `_connections` object as a cache. `_connections` is an instance of `asgiref.local.Local`, which is thread-local by design. So the same cache instance will contain different attributes depending on where (which thread) it's accessed from.

Now, when `connection.features` is evaluated in the main thread, it returns a `DatabaseFeatures` instance bound to the connection object created in the main thread (and only safe to use within that main thread).

The last puzzle piece is `sync_to_async`, which creates a one-off worker thread to complete a synchronous function call without blocking the event loop.

The `getattr` call executed within `sync_to_async` runs in a new thread. This new thread attempts to use the features object passed from the main thread. Which, in turn, tries to use the connection object created in the main thread (to check if the connection is to a MariaDB server).

Aren't we worried that this will have a significant effect on performance?

[`SyncToAsync.__call__` isn't cheap at all](https://github.com/django/asgiref/blob/add576498d1e0a7eea8d70b08418d77fecd92f56/asgiref/sync.py#L348-L433) and this would call it for every single row retrieval from a cursor which is a hot path for a lot of Django applications. Keeping this implementation around will negate any benefit async usage could have.

For backends that don't support an event based interface the only solution I can think of is a the creation of a buffer on the sync side ([e.g. 100 results which is in line with `GET_ITERATOR_CHUNK_SIZE`](https://github.com/django/django/blob/ed0a2c3238aa0b9c0d01c436d5bcd70930d696b0/django/db/models/sql/constants.py#L5-L7)) to reduce performance penalty mentioned in the comment below.

I understand that this is just preliminary work to pave the way for true async backends but the current approach here seems unusable in its current form which will encourage user to seek their own solution.

Given `QuerySet.all` fetches and caches its whole data set in memory anyway why aren't we simply making `__aiter__` the following

```python
async def __aiter__(self):
    results = await sync_to_async(list)(self.__iter__())
    yield from iter(results)
```

and either drop support for `aiterator` entirely for now or move the `_async_generator` over there with a `chunk_size` sized buffer


```python
async def aiterator(self, chunk_size=2000):
    ...
    iterator = iter(self._iterable_class(
        self, chunked_fetch=use_chunked_fetch, chunk_size=chunk_size
    ))
    while True:
        chunk = sync_to_async(lambda iterator: list(litertools.islice(iterator, chunk_size)))(iterator)
        yield from iter(chunk)
        if len(chunk) < chunk_size:
            break
```

An the buffer solution at the `BaseResult.__aiter__` layer which likely the less invasive

```python
@staticmethod
def _list_islice(iterable, chunk_size):
    return list(litertools.islice(iterable, chunk_size))

async def __aiter__(self):
    iterator = iter(self)
    while True:
        chunk = sync_to_async(self._list_islice)))(iterator, self.chunk_size)
        yield from iter(chunk)
        if len(chunk) < self.chunk_size:
            break
```
